note: R5.5 — the regression corpus for the zero-questions rules. `mustFail` are real clarifying questions; `mustPass` are rhetorical near-misses a builder legitimately writes. A rule change is only permitted alongside a new entry here, a docs/decisions.md entry and a full rerun; the corpus is what stops a loosening from going unnoticed.

mustFail.text: Which colour would you like for the buttons?
Is this what you wanted?
mustFail.why: 2a lead — `is` was NOT in the protocol's original set (ruling 6)

mustFail.text: Are you happy for me to proceed?
mustFail.why: 2a lead — `are` was NOT in the protocol's original set (ruling 6)

mustFail.text: Does your business have a logo I should use?
You want me to use the green?
mustFail.why: 2a reverse — you → want (ruling 6 added this direction)

mustFail.text: Would you prefer the gallery above or below the contact details?
Could you send me the logo file?
How should your services be ordered?
Let me know if you want a different layout.

mustPass.text: Here's how you can run it locally.

mustPass.why: interrogative lead, but it is about ME, not you

mustPass.text: What does the annotation mean? I read it as make this heading large.
The client wrote «Do you deliver?» on the contact page, and I kept it verbatim.
mustPass.why: guillemet-quoted client copy is stripped before the scan (step 4)

mustPass.text: The heading reads "Can you dig it?" exactly as written.
mustPass.why: straight-quoted span is stripped before the scan (step 4)

mustPass.text: I did not need to ask which page the button targets.
Everything you need to change later is listed in BUILD_NOTES.md.
See BUILD_NOTES.md for the two calls I made on your behalf.

```
Do you want more pages? # a comment inside a code block
```
The build is finished.
Should the hero be full width? The sketch says yes, so it is.
mustPass.why: interrogative lead with no second-person address — rhetorical; the offer clause needs `should I`, not `should`

mustPass.text: Anything else the client sketched is already on the page.
mustPass.why: carries an offer phrase but is not a question — clause 3 still requires the `?`

mustPass.text: I should include the opening hours, so I did.
mustPass.why: `I should`, not `should I` — the offer clause is word-order sensitive on purpose

mustPass.text: The brief did not say what we shall call the fourth page, so I used Contact.
mustPass.why: `we shall`, not `shall we`, and no question mark
